graph.name: desk-led
graph.description: Desk LED: a coin cell, a push button and an LED on one small board – press the button and the LED lights.

purpose.notes: A small board for the owner's own desk in Austria, built and used by the owner – not sold or given away (D-1). Powered by a coin cell; no mains, no radio.

conventions.pin_reference: '<designator>.<pin>' with the pin's name or role, else its symbol number – the parts entry says which pin that is
conventions.v: per net: [min, max] in V over all operating states
conventions.accept: per net or component: {code: reason} accepts a finding on purpose (edakit explain <code>)

components.label: CR2032 holder
components.notes: Pin 1 = plus, pin 2 = minus (HanElectricity drawing Rev. A, footprint '+' at pad 1). SMD, placed by JLCPCB in Economic assembly (R-3, D-3).

accept.LIM.i/cell: SW1 is pressed for a moment: while it is held a fresh cell gives up to 4.0 mA, above its 3 mA continuous and below its 15 mA pulse current (Jauch CR 2032 H2B); held longer it costs capacity and voltage, no harm – the voltage drop is in the simulation by the cell's r (D-3)

components.label: Push button 12 × 12 mm
components.notes: Pins 1/2 and 3/4 are connected inside (Kinghelm drawing p. 7). Wired on the diagonal 1 and 4, so it works whichever way the pairs run – the drawing does not number the pads (M-1 review, note 5).

components.label: LED series resistor
components.notes: 330 Ω: from a fresh cell at most 4.0 mA into D1 (lowest VF), from a used cell (2.5 V, 40 Ω) into a D1 of the highest VF bin below 1 mA – still lit; 270 Ω would give 0.97 mA there and 5 mA fresh, no real gain (sim, D-3, D-4).

components.label: LED (green 0805)
components.notes: AlInGaP green, VF 1.9–2.4 V at 20 mA – an InGaN green (2.6–3.1 V) stays dark on a used CR2032 (D-3).

nets.name: VBAT
nets.notes: the cell: 3.0 V nominal, 3.2 V and a little more fresh off load; negative with the cell upside down

nets.name: LED_SW
nets.notes: the cell's voltage while SW1 is pressed

accept.PATH.reverse: a cell upside down drives R1 and D1 backwards: D1 blocks, 3.2 V against its VR of 5 V – sim scenario reversed/pressed (LIM.v reverse voltage, SIM.state LED dark); a Schottky in series would cost the 0.3 V the used cell needs (D-3)

notes: the cell (Ø 20 mm) stands out of BT1 (16 mm wide) on both long sides: keep them free, with room to lever the cell out
BT1's drawing hatches 11 × 7 mm between its pads: no copper and no vias there
D1 next to SW1: the LED shows the press
silkscreen beside BT1: a '+' and the cell's outline, so the cell goes in plus side up – the holder takes it either way, and upside down it may stay dark or short (M-1 review, note 1)
board size: fit to the parts (D-1)

accept.HINT.bulk: no cable and no plug: the cell sits in BT1 on the board, the only load is D1 (at most 4.0 mA)
accept.HINT.lithium: a CR2032 is a primary Li-MnO2 cell, not Li-ion: nothing on the board charges it (LIM.backfeed) and it is not recharged
